title: Mean corpuscular volume (MCV)

review.note: Drafted from the source below; not yet reviewed by a medical professional.

measures: Mean corpuscular volume (MCV) measures the average size of your red blood cells. It is one of the red blood cell indices reported as part of a complete blood count.
context: MCV is used with other red blood cell indices and blood tests to help tell apart different types of anemia. One index alone is not enough to make a diagnosis.
aboveRange: Red blood cells larger than usual, which can be associated with anemia caused by a vitamin B deficiency
Can be associated with liver conditions
belowRange: Red blood cells smaller than usual, which can be associated with iron deficiency anemia
Can be associated with thalassemia, a group of inherited blood disorders
nextStep: Discuss this result with your doctor.
